photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CAN 6 – FIN 3 (Bronze Medal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Gavin McKenna finished with a goal and three assists, Michael Hage recorded four helpers, Zayne Parekh made history and Canada’s National Junior Team doubled up Finland 6-3 to win the bronze medal at the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship in Saint Paul, Minnesota.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: McKenna (1G 3A) and Hage (4A) led Canada to the bronze medal.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CZE 6 – CAN 4 (Semifinal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Jack Ivankovic was terrific in a 31-save performance and Canada’s National Junior Team erased a trio of deficits, but it fell just short in a 6-4 loss to Czechs in the semifinals of the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship in Saint Paul, Minnesota.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Ivankovic made 31 saves, but Canada was edged by the Czechs.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CAN 7 – SVK 1 (Quarterfinal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Seven players scored goals, 14 recorded points and Canada’s National Junior Team scored five goals in 5:49 in the first period to beat Slovakia 7-1 and move into the semifinals at the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Fourteen players recorded points to help Canada move into the semis.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CAN 7 – FIN 4 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Cole Beaudoin and Brady Martin scored two goals apiece, and Canada’s National Junior Team pulled away over the final 40 minutes to beat Finland 7-4 and clinch first place in Group B at the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Beaudoin and Martin scored 2G each to lead Canada atop Group B.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CAN 9 – DEN 1 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Gavin McKenna scored a hat trick, Brady Martin set up all three and Canada’s National Junior Team kept its unbeaten record intact in Group B at the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 9-1 win over Denmark in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: McKenna scored a hat trick to help Canada stay unbeaten in Group B.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CAN 2 – LAT 1 OT (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Michael Hage was the overtime hero, scoring on the power play just 44 seconds into the extra period as Canada’s National Junior Team made it two wins in as many days at the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 2-1 victory over Latvia.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Hage scored 44 seconds into OT to lead the Canadians to a second win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CAN 7 – CZE 5 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Zayne Parekh scored twice, Michael Hage and Ethan MacKenzie had a goal and two assists apiece and Canada’s National Junior Team outlasted Czechia 7-5 to open the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship with a win in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Parekh scored 2G to help Canada outlast the Czechs in the opener.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: SWE 4 – CAN 2 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Tij Iginla and Braeden Cootes scored goals in the second period, but Canada’s National Junior Team finished with a split of its two game pre-tournament series with Sweden ahead of the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship after a 4-2 loss in London, Ontario.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Iginla and Cootes scored, but Canada was doubled up by the Swedes.

photosToDisplay.title: 2026 WJC: CAN 2 – SWE 1 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Brady Martin scored two goals, Gavin McKenna set up both and Canada’s National Junior Team opened its exhibition schedule ahead of the 2026 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 2-1 win over Sweden in Kitchener, Ontario.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Martin scored both goals to lead Canada to a victory in Kitchener.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: CZE 4 – CAN 3 (Quarterfinal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Tanner Howe, Porter Martone and Bradly Nadeau scored, but a last-minute goal was the difference as Canada’s National Junior Team fell 4-3 to Czechia in the quarterfinals at the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Nadeau tied it with 4:18 left, but Canada was eliminated by the Czechs.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: USA 4 – CAN 1 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Bradly Nadeau scored on a third-period power play and Carter George made 24 saves, but Canada’s National Junior Team dropped a 4-1 decision to the United States to close prelim play at the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Nadeau scored on a third-period PP, but Canada fell to the Americans.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: CAN 3 – GER 0 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Carter George made 25 saves for his second-straight shutout, Oliver Bonk scored on a first-period power play and Canada’s National Junior Team got back into the win column at the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship, beating Germany 3-0.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: George made 25 saves for the SO to help Canada blank the Germans.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: LAT 3 – CAN 2 SO (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Jett Luchanko scored shorthanded, Calum Ritchie had a power-play goal and Canada’s National Junior Team racked up 56 shots on goal, but it dropped a 3-2 decision to Latvia in an eight-round shootout at the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Luchanko and Ritchie scored, but Canada was edged in a shootout.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: CAN 4 – FIN 0 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Carter George posted a 31-save shutout, Matthew Schaefer had a goal and an assist and Canada’s National Junior Team got preliminary-round play at the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship underway with a 4-0 win over Finland.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: George earned a 31-save SO, backstopping Canada past the Finns.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: CAN 3 – CZE 2 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Gavin McKenna scored twice, including the game-winning goal with just 2:29 left, as Canada’s National Junior Team closed out pre-tournament play ahead of the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 3-2 win over Czechia.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: McKenna scored 2G, including a late GWG, to give Canada the victory.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: CAN 4 – SWE 2 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Easton Cowan scored a hat trick, 12 players put their names on the scoresheet and Canada’s National Junior Team opened its pre-tournament schedule ahead of the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 7-1 win over Switzerland.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Cowan had a hat trick to lead Canada to a pre-World Juniors win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2025 WJC: CAN 7 – SUI 1 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Easton Cowan scored a hat trick, 12 players put their names on the scoresheet and Canada’s National Junior Team opened its pre-tournament schedule ahead of the 2025 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 7-1 win over Switzerland.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Cowan had a hat trick to lead Canada to a pre-World Juniors win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2024 NJT Selection Camp: Canada 2, U SPORTS 1
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Brayden Yager had a two-point performance in Canada’s 2-1 win over the U SPORTS all-stars in the National Junior Team selection camp finale at TD Place in Ottawa, Ontario.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Brayden Yager's two-point performance led Canada past the U SPORTS all-stars.

photosToDisplay.title: 2024 NJT Selection Camp: Canada 5, U SPORTS 2
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Carson Rehkopf netted a hat trick and Beckett Sennecke recorded two assists in Canada’s 5-2 win over the U SPORTS all-stars during National Junior Team selection camp at TD Place in Ottawa, Ontario.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Carson Rehkopf netted a hat trick in Canada’s first game against the U SPORTS all-stars.

photosToDisplay.title: 2024 WJC: CAN 5 - FIN 2 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob:
Nate Danielson and Maveric Lamoureux had a goal and an assist each and Mathis Rousseau made
24 saves as Canada’s National Junior Team opened preliminary-round play at the 2024 IIHF World
Junior Championship with a 5-2 win over Finland on Boxing Day.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Danielson and Lamoureux had 1G 1A each in a Boxing Day win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CAN 4 – SVK 3 OT (Quarterfinal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Connor Bedard made history with a first-period goal and ended it with a beauty in overtime as Canada’s National Junior Team edged Slovakia 4-3 in overtime to move into the semifinals at the 2023 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Bedard scored twice, including a beauty in OT, to push Canada to the semis.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CAN 6 – USA 2 (Semifinals)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Joshua Roy scored twice and added two assists, Thomas Milic made 43 saves, and Canada’s National Junior Team booked its ticket to the gold medal game after defeating the United States 6-2 in the semifinals of the 2023 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Joshua Roy notched four points as Canada defeated the United States.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CZE 2 – CAN 3 OT (Gold Medal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Dylan Guenther was the overtime hero 6:22 into the extra period, and Canada claimed a 20th gold medal at the IIHF World Junior Championship with a 3-2 win over Czechia.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Guenther was the overtime hero, giving Canada a 20th gold medal.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CAN 5 – SWE 1 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Brennan Othmann scored twice, Connor Bedard had four assists, and Canada’s National Junior Team defeated Sweden 5-1 to finish the preliminary round at the 2023 IIHF World Junior Championship, booking a quarterfinal matchup against Slovakia.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Othmann scored twice to help Canada close the prelims with a win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CAN 11 – AUT 0 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Connor Bedard inched closer to history with two goals and four assists, and 10 different players found the back of the net as Canada’s National Junior Team blanked Austria 11-0 on Thursday night at the 2023 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Ten different players scored goals as Canada blanked the Austrians.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CAN 11 – GER 2 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Connor Bedard tied a Canadian record with seven points, Dylan Guenther scored a hat trick and Canada’s National Junior Team got into the win column at the 2023 IIHF World Junior Championship, beating Germany 11-2.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Hat tricks from Bedard and Guenther propelled Canada past Germany.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CZE 5 – CAN 2 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Shane Wright and Connor Bedard scored goals and Thomas Milic stopped all 10 shots in relief, but Canada’s National Junior Team dropped a 5-2 decision to Czechia in its opener at the 2023 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Wright and Bedard scored, but Canada dropped its prelim opener.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CAN 6 – SVK 1 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Joshua Roy had a goal and an assist, while Shane Wright and Caedan Bankier added two helpers apiece as Canada’s National Junior Team earned a 6-1 win over Slovakia in pre-tournament action ahead of the 2023 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Roy had a goal and an assist to help Canada past the Slovaks.

photosToDisplay.title: 2023 WJC: CAN 6 – SUI 0 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Shane Wright scored twice, and Connor Bedard had a three-point night as Canada shut out Switzerland 6-0 in its first pre-tournament game in Moncton, N.B., ahead of the 2023 World Juniors.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Shane Wright scored twice to lead Canada to shut out Switzerland.

photosToDisplay.title: 2022 WJC: CAN 4 – SWE 3 (Pre-Tournament)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Nathan Gaucher and Mason McTavish scored 34 seconds apart to get the offence going, and Canada’s National Junior Team held off a late push to earn a 4-3 pre-tournament victory over Sweden ahead of the 2022 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Gaucher and MacTavish scored 0:34 apart early, and Canada held on.

photosToDisplay.title: 2022 WJC: CAN 5 – LAT 2 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Lukas Cormier, Olen Zellweger and Ridly Greig scored in the back half of the second period to open up a three-goal lead, helping Canada’s National Junior Team open its schedule at the 2022 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 5-2 win over Latvia.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Bedard and Greig finished with 1G 1A apiece as Canada opened with a win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2022 WJC: CAN 11 – SVK 1 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Captain Mason McTavish tied the goals record with a four-goal game and two assists as Canada beat Slovakia 11-1 on Thursday at the 2022 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: McTavish had a six point game as Canada beat Slovakia on Thursday.

photosToDisplay.title: 2022 WJC: CAN 6 – FIN 3 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Mason McTavish had a goal and two assists to add to his tournament-leading totals, Olen Zellweger set up a trio of goals and Canada’s National Junior Team downed Finland 6-3 to finish a perfect preliminary round and clinch first place in Group A at the 2022 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Zellweger set up three goals as Canada finished a perfect prelims.

photosToDisplay.title: 2022 WJC: CAN 3 – FIN 2 OT (Gold)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Kent Johnson was the overtime hero, scoring the game-winning goal 3:20 minutes into extra time and Canada beat Finland 3-2 to win its 19th IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Johnson scored in OT to give Canada its 19th World Juniors victory.

photosToDisplay.title: WJC: Three masks, two Team Canadas
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Check out the goalie masks designed by – and featuring – Canada’s National Women’s Team goaltenders that will be worn by the Team Canada puck-stoppers at the 2022 IIHF World Junior Championship as part of the Janes ALL IN program.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Check out the special masks that will be worn at the World Juniors.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021-22 NJT: CAN 7 – USP 2 (Exhibition)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Seven players scored goals and 13 recorded at least a point as Canada’s National Junior Team campers closed selection camp with a 7-2 win over U SPORTS.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Seven players scored goals as Canada closed selection camp with a win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021-22 NJT: CAN 3 – USP 0 (Exhibition)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Connor Bedard scored twice and added an assist, and Sebastian Cossa posted a 29-save shutout as Canada’s National Junior Team hopefuls downed U SPORTS 3-0 in the opener at selection camp.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Bedard posted 2G 1A to give Canada the first win at selection camp.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021-22 POE: WHT 9 – RED 8 (Intrasquad)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Corson Ceulemans scored 51 seconds in OT, Logan Stankoven and Kent Johnson had two goals each and White outlasted Red 9-8 in the in the second of two junior/under-18 combined games at the POE Summer Showcase.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Ceulemans scored 51 seconds into OT to give White a wild win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021-22 POE: RED 7 – WHT 2 (Intrasquad)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Zachary Bolduc scored twice in the first period and added an assist, and Garin Bjorklund made 37 saves to lead Red to a 7-2 win over White in the first of two junior/under-18 combined games at the POE Summer Showcase.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Bolduc scored twice in the first period to help Red to the win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021-22 NJT: WHT 2 – RED 1 (Intrasquad)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Zachary L’Heureux and Dylan Guenther scored the goals, Dylan Garand and Brett Brochu combined for 33 saves and White edged Red 2-1 to earn a split of the intrasquad series at Canada’s National Junior Team summer camp.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Zachary L’Heureux scored the winner to get White the series split.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021-22 NJT: RED 4 – WHT 2 (Intrasquad)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Cole Perfetti’s power-play goal late in the second period stood up as the game-winner as Red doubled up White 4-2 to open intrasquad play at Canada’s National Junior Team summer camp.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Perfetti’s power-play goal helped Red to the first intrasquad win.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: Frame by Frame – Around the rink
photosToDisplay.textBlob:
Check out the best candid Canadian moments at the World Juniors.
Get an inside look at Canada’s National Junior Team on the ice and in the dressing room with candid moments from practices, warm-ups and more at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Get an inside look at Team Canada on the ice and in the dressing room with candid moments from the World Juniors.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: Frame by Frame – Behind the scenes
photosToDisplay.textBlob:
Pull back the curtain and see what happened off the ice at the World Juniors.
Pull back the curtain and check out what happened off the ice at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship through the eyes of the teams, Hockey Canada, the International Ice Hockey Federation and volunteers.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Go behind the scenes at the World Juniors through the eyes of the teams, Hockey Canada, the IIHF and volunteers.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: Frame by Frame – Game action
photosToDisplay.textBlob:
Look back at the best moments from Canada’s run at the World Juniors.
From Boxing Day against Germany to the gold medal game against the United States, look back at the best moments from Canada’s seven-game run at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: From Boxing Day to the gold medal game, look back at the best moments from Canada’s run at the World Juniors.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: USA 2 – CAN 0 (Gold Medal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Devon Levi capped a Top Goaltender performance with 19 saves and Canada’s National Junior Team outshot the United States 34-21, but it couldn’t find the back of the net in a 2-0 gold medal game loss at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Canada outshot the Americans 34-21, but was left with a silver medal.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: CAN 5 – RUS 0 (Semifinal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Devon Levi tied the all-time WJC record with his third shutout of the tournament, Dylan Cozens added three more points and Canada’s National Junior Team blanked Russia 5-0 to book its spot in the gold medal game at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Levi and Cozens led Canada past Russia and into the gold medal game.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: CAN 3 – CZE 0 (Quarterfinal)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Devon Levi was brilliant in a 29-save shutout performance, a trio of returnees provided the offence and Canada’s National Junior Team moved into the semifinals at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 3-0 win over the Czech Republic.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Levi was brilliant, making 29 saves to send Canada to the semifinals.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: CAN 4 - FIN 1 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Dylan Cozens opened and closed the scoring to take over the tournament scoring lead, helping Canada’s National Junior Team down Finland 4-1 to cap a perfect preliminary round and finish atop Group A at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Cozens opened and closed the scoring to help Canada atop Group A.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: CAN 10 – SUI 0 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Quinton Byfield broke out with two goals and four assists, Devon Levi earned a 15-save shutout and Canada’s National Junior Team made it three-for-three at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship with a 10-0 win over Switzerland.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Byfield finished with two goals and four assists in a shutout victory.

photosToDisplay.title: 2021 WJC: CAN 3 – SVK 1 (Preliminary)
photosToDisplay.textBlob: Jordan Spence, Philip Tomasino and Jack Quinn provided the offence to help Canada’s National Junior Team hold off a pesky Slovakian side and earn a 3-1 win to remain perfect atop Group A at the 2021 IIHF World Junior Championship.
photosToDisplay.shortDescription: Spence, Tomasino and Quinn scored to help Canada edge the Slovaks.

videosToDisplay.Title: WJC: Highlights - CAN 6 USA 2 (Semifinals)
videosToDisplay.ShortDescription: Milic réalise 43 arrêts pour mener le Canada jusqu’en finale.
videosToDisplay.LongDescription: Joshua Roy a touché la cible à deux reprises en plus de récolter deux mentions d’aide, Thomas Milic a effectué 43 arrêts, et l’équipe nationale junior du Canada a inscrit les six derniers buts de la partie pour signer une victoire de 6-2 face aux États-Unis en demi-finale du Championnat mondial junior 2023 de l’IIHF. Le Canada obtient donc son laissez-passer pour le match pour la médaille d’or.
